summary.headline: JSW Infrastructure Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 16% YoY to INR674 crores on 31 MT cargo; FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR3,000 crores reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating revenue rose 18% YoY to INR1,445 crores and operating EBITDA rose 16% to INR674 crores, with cargo up 6% to 31 MT. Fujairah contributed negligibly due to Middle East disruption; excluding Fujairah, India cargo grew 11%. PAT fell to INR358 crores from INR390 crores as other income dropped and ETR rose. Management revised FY27 cargo guidance to about 127 MT (excluding Fujairah) and reaffirmed FY27 EBITDA guidance of about INR3,000 crores and FY28 of INR5,000 crores. A INR7,503 crore QIP closed and Moody's upgraded the rating to Baa3.

segments.name: Ports
segments.commentary: Cargo 31 MT (+6% YoY); port revenue INR1,208 crores (+11%) and EBITDA INR601 crores (+7%), margin 49.8% vs 51.8%, mainly due to Fujairah volume loss. Excluding Fujairah, India cargo grew 11%.

segments.name: Logistics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR237 crores vs INR138 crores; EBITDA INR73 crores vs INR20 crores, margin 30.6% vs 14.5%. Navkar domestic cargo 385,000 tonnes (+40%) and EXIM 83,000 TEUs (+2%). Rail rakes contributed INR43 crores revenue and INR40 crores EBITDA on net-basis accounting.

segments.name: Fujairah
segments.commentary: Negligible contribution in Q1 due to Middle East operating environment; 8 tanks expected operational by end July or early August 2026, with 3 more targeted around September or October.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of about INR3,000 crores reaffirmed; FY28 guidance of INR5,000 crores reaffirmed.
FY27 cargo volume guidance revised to about 127 MT, net of lost Fujairah cargo.
Fujairah baked into FY27 EBITDA guidance at about INR100-125 crores, with about 2-2.5 MT of volume.
Capacity target raised to 300 MTPA by FY28 and 400 MTPA by FY30 or earlier.
Capex of about INR16,500 crores planned for FY27-FY28 (INR13,000 crores ports, INR3,500 crores logistics); INR6,900 crores spent to June 2026 and INR5,500 crores further committed.
Rake fleet to reach about 250 rakes (about 110 rail and 140 container) in 2-3 years; 40 new rakes expected by Jan-Feb 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of geopolitical crisis on cost escalation for under-construction projects such as the slurry pipeline.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no ongoing projects were affected; only intermittent LPG and diesel availability issues, absorbed in contingency within the total project cost.

qa_highlights.question: What would Q1 port EBITDA have been without Fujairah disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said port EBITDA would have been about INR670-675 crores vs INR601 crores, i.e. roughly INR65-70 crores incremental after FX benefit, with INR8 crores Fujairah expense already in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 volume and EBITDA guidance still on track and how much Fujairah is baked in?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume guidance revised to about 127 MT excluding Fujairah; EBITDA guidance of INR3,000 crores retained, with Fujairah contributing about INR100-125 crores and 2-2.5 MT.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential port margin improvement and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it mainly to Jaigarh cargo mix (alumina and project cargo), plus SWPL and Dharamtar volume growth; said the alumina and project cargo elements are not recurring, while LPG cargo is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Keni port clearance and Murbe construction start?
qa_highlights.answer: Keni applied at Karnataka Coastal Zone Management Authority; expected 3-4 months to EC after forwarding to MoEF&CC. Murbe EC covers the entire project including DFC connectivity; construction expected around December-January, concession agreement in 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance recovery and Fujairah normalisation timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Claims filed; resolution expected by end-October 2026. Eight Fujairah tanks ready by end-July or early August; management said operations depend on market conditions and ship arrivals.

qa_highlights.question: Other income fall and treasury outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income fell due to lower treasury balances from equity funding of capex; QIP proceeds received by June 30 should lift treasury income for the rest of the year. Q4 FY26 included about INR40 crores interest received from Hiranandani JV partner on Jaigarh receivables.

capex_capacity: Capex of about INR16,500 crores planned for FY27-FY28, of which about INR13,000 crores for ports and INR3,500 crores for logistics; cumulative outlay about INR6,900 crores up to June 2026, including INR671 crores spent in Q1; a further INR5,500 crores already committed via orders for machinery, long-lead items and civil work.

Capacity currently 186 MTPA, targeted at 300 MTPA by FY28 and 400 MTPA by FY30 or earlier; Kolkata container capacity to about 1.4 million TEUs on completion of Outer Container Terminal and Berths 1-5 PPP project (Berths 7-8 first phase).

Slurry pipeline: 251 km of pipeline lowered (about 83% execution), on track for completion by March 2027. Murbe (Maharashtra) received environmental clearance and DFC rail connectivity approval; construction expected to start around December 2026 to January 2027. Keni port EC expected in about 3-4 months after state coastal authority forwards to MoEF&CC.

Jatadhar Port (Odisha) construction in full swing after Novation agreement with anchor customer. South West Port Goa consent to operate for 12 MTPA (from 11). Mangalore container terminal capacity raised to 6 MTPA from 4.2 MTPA. Tuticorin Bulk Terminal on track; Jaigarh and Dharamtar brownfield expansions progressing.

Fujairah: 8 tanks expected operational by end-July or early August 2026, with 3 more targeted around September-October 2026. Rakes: fleet of 42 (25 rail, 17 container) with 40 new rakes (15 rail, 25 container) ordered April 2026; first two rail rakes received in July, balance by Jan-Feb 2027; target fleet about 250 rakes (about 110 rail and 140 container) over 2-3 years.
demand_pricing: Cargo 31 MT in Q1 FY27 (+6% YoY vs 29.4 MT); India operations ex-Fujairah grew 11% YoY. Fujairah third-party volumes fell 48% and contributed negligibly.

Port revenue INR1,208 crores (+11% YoY), driven by volume growth and favourable product mix; port EBITDA INR601 crores (+7%), margin 49.8% vs 51.8% YoY, attributed to lost Fujairah volume. Management said Fujairah-related drag was about INR65-70 crores of EBITDA in the quarter.
Q1 one-offs: Jaigarh alumina and project cargo (non-recurring per management) and INR8-9 crores one-time crane shifting cost at Jaigarh. Incremental LPG cargo at Jaigarh expected to continue.

Logistics: Navkar domestic cargo 385,000 tonnes (+40%), EXIM 83,000 TEUs (+2%); Navkar revenue INR191 crores (+38%). Rail rakes contributed INR43 crores revenue and INR40 crores EBITDA on net-basis accounting; management said margin on gross basis would be about 25%.

FY27 cargo guidance revised to about 127 MT excluding Fujairah; FY27 EBITDA guidance INR3,000 crores includes Fujairah at about INR100-125 crores EBITDA and 2-2.5 MT volume. Rake utilisation mix is about 75% third-party and 25% group today; Murbe cargo expected about 80% third-party and 20% group.

Kolkata (Phase 1, Berths 7-8) steady-state EBITDA guided at about INR70-90 crores on prevailing NSRs; full 1.4 million TEU project about INR300-350 crores EBITDA; existing Kolkata facilities at about 90% utilisation.
risks_watch: Fujairah recovery depends on Middle East conditions and ship arrivals; 8 tanks targeted by early August and 3 more by September-October 2026, with the insurance claim resolution targeted by end-October 2026.
Port EBITDA margin fell to 49.8% from 51.8%; Q1 included non-recurring Jaigarh alumina and project cargo and INR8-9 crores one-off crane shifting cost, so sustainability of margin is uncertain.
Keni port EC timeline (3-4 months post state forwarding) and KCZMA delays already pushed the project by about a year; Keni and Murbe third-party ramp-up depends on greenfield execution.
Rake deliveries: only 2 of 40 ordered rakes received so far; remaining rakes due by Jan-Feb 2027; GPWIS moratorium may affect the 250-rake target.
Navkar merger plan undecided; NCR Rail terminal bid expected to close in Q2 FY27 and NCLT asset bids under consideration.
Oman port concession agreement still pending conditions precedent; expected in one to two months.
key_quotes: Excluding Fujairah, our India operations recorded an impressive 11% year-on-year growth in cargo volumes, significantly outpacing overall industry growth and validating the strength of our business model and deep customer relationships.
We should deliver you a number of around 127 million tonnes this year.
Stick to our guidance of INR3,000 crores, Priyankar, in terms of the EBITDA.
These are in this quarter, especially the ones on alumina and project cargo were there in this quarter, but I don't think this will be recurring in nature.

Given the strong operating momentum and execution progress across ports and logistics, we reaffirm our operating EBITDA guidance of approximately INR3,000 crores for FY27 and INR5,000 crores for FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, capacity and EBITDA guidance (reaffirmed INR3,000 crores FY27 and INR5,000 crores FY28) while noting Fujairah uncertainty. Management was cautious and deferential on Fujairah timing and insurance recovery, and gave no precise figures on Navkar merger or acquisitions beyond pipeline status.
